scope: Original technical findings and comparison contracts; no raw community posts or private provenance locators.

findings.title: Dynamic color needs allocated RGB storage
findings.evidence: Source and original-binary inspections plus new development diagnostic/tests; controlled retail runtime case pending
findings.finding: Inspect actual proposed JKL rows and final float32 values. A source-preserving export may retain scalar rows even when regenerated MotS rows use independent white and RGB channels. The inspected retail four-channel compaction branch ignores blue in its equality predicate.
findings.action: Use schema vertexColors / vertex-colors in builds exposing the new report-first diagnostic, or MCP sed_diagnose kind vertexColors. Validate equal channels, blue-only and white-only differences, one differing corner, grey/recolor and rebake before any automatic preparation.
findings.qualification: Not proof of scalar-row behavior, all executable versions, or runtime parity. Do not set a flag alone or globally perturb levels.

findings.title: Preserve independent white and RGB authoring
findings.finding: Explicit equal or zero RGB source-light values retain their independence; null can mean inherit white. Historical metadata is not necessarily an engine falloff parameter.
findings.action: Query stored/effective channels, preserve omission semantics, and verify save/reopen and unselected samples.
findings.qualification: Preservation is not recalculated lighting or engine proof.

findings.title: Distinguish existing world occlusion from future model shadows
findings.evidence: Current editor source and maintained documentation
findings.finding: Supported builds already offer unoccluded source-point and world-polygon-occluded ARCH recipes with resource/provenance guards.
findings.action: Compare transforms, normals, samples, BlockLight and NoBlock on original fixtures; separately scope model/self/alpha-aware shadowing and animation.
findings.qualification: Single-LOD rest-pose recipes do not establish general renderer or retail parity.

findings.title: Compare the announced C++ editor one feature at a time
findings.evidence: Author announcement carried in private research; checked public source availability
findings.finding: A forthcoming Qt/C++ SED replacement and MotS ARCH authoring were reported. The checked public SED source remains the Delphi line; no replacement build/source was obtained in that bounded check.
findings.action: On an actual release, pin source/build, establish lineage and compare original UV, geometry, ARCH, frame and automation fixtures independently.
findings.qualification: Announcement, demonstration, source delivery and runtime verification remain distinct; later source may change current availability.

findings.title: Runtime preview must acknowledge the applied revision
findings.finding: The WDFUSE renderer sends its HTTP response before applying full/partial geometry and object changes. Transport receipt therefore cannot prove an editor update was applied.
findings.action: Use capability negotiation and separate received/applied/observed revisions with explicit resource and scene identities.
findings.qualification: WDFUSE is a Dark Forces precedent, not Sith format support or an existing SED runtime bridge.

findings.title: Expose engine diagnostics through declared capabilities
findings.finding: Editor-mode engine paths contain COG trace/list/status/pause and AI status/list commands. Their presence in source does not establish enablement in a chosen runtime or MCP exposure.
findings.action: Discover supported observer/debug operations explicitly; keep observation separate from deliberate runtime mutation and retain binary identity.
findings.qualification: No new interactive debugger or remote interface was executed by this research.

findings.title: COG editing must preserve message fallthrough
findings.evidence: Language behavior and reviewed editor-design correction
findings.finding: Splitting a script into independent editable message bodies can change semantics when labels fall through or share code.
findings.action: Keep a source-order-preserving document model; make outlines and typed binding views projections of that model.
findings.qualification: A placed-script binding editor is not a complete source IDE.

findings.title: Build reference graphs on exact typed bindings
findings.evidence: Current shared binding model and historical workflow analysis
findings.finding: A queryable reference graph can support both graphical pick-target actions and agents without substituting names for exact runtime/resource identities.
findings.action: Preserve ordered COG serialization, script hashes and explicit remapping during geometry/object edits.
findings.qualification: Static links do not prove lifetime or identity after difficulty filtering and runtime object recycling.

findings.title: Incremental scene edits need explicit invalidation
findings.finding: A persistent viewport must decide which geometry, instances, materials, light samples and acceleration structures become stale after each edit.
findings.action: Specify dirty regions and supported incremental operations; rebuild or refuse unsupported combinations with an applied-revision receipt.
findings.qualification: A network wrapper alone does not solve scene lifetime or synchronization.

findings.title: Mesh preview is not sector decomposition
findings.evidence: Tool scope and topology comparison analysis
findings.finding: An imported object/hierarchy or geometry export does not automatically create valid convex sector volumes, reciprocal adjoins, templates or a playable episode.
findings.action: For decomposition require a closed defined input, whole-mesh success, topology/reference preservation and atomic refusal on partial failure.
findings.qualification: Blender-Sith is an asset toolkit; do not imply general solid subtraction or full level-authoring coverage from a geometry demonstration.

findings.title: Use original bounded recipes for agent-generated detail
findings.evidence: Existing bounded placement arrays and procedural-script analysis
findings.finding: Placing model things within sectors is different from generating new sectors. Reproducible brushes/scatter need a seed, accepted samples, resource identity and a reference/topology diff.
findings.action: Reuse shared arrays and selections, then add explicit clearance/containment policy and human/agent equivalent undo where justified.
findings.qualification: Point containment is not collision clearance or gameplay pathfinding.

findings.title: Keep similarly named editors and libraries distinct
findings.finding: Delphi SED, an announced C++ rewrite, NJED, NED/Smith, Mudhorn and separate material/lighting tools have different code availability and runtime targets.
findings.action: Track exact owner/repository/version, license, acquisition hash, inspected files and the specific portable behavior rather than treating every screenshot as the same editor.
findings.qualification: Missing source in checked routes is a bounded result; availability can change.
